items.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: I got Eddie Jones in the band, Bill Hughes, Sonny Cohn, Eric Dixon, Thad Jones... Yeah I got a whole lot of people in the band, you know.

ctx.x: What was it like playing in different parts of the world with the Basie band?

Oh, we always had a good following. And the band was hot. We were in one of the best bands Basie ever had. And that’s the band that made him rich, you know. The band was tight. I had forgotten actually, how good the band was until I was listening to those Mosaic recordings. And then it came back to me, how good that band was. It was like one person playing, you know. Everybody was—it was a good band. Well Basie, he knew how to do that. You know he didn’t fault nobody. He just let it stay there until the cats got…
Were you happy switching from the tenor to the alto?

items.title: Frank Wess — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We go back that far, and we affiliate, off and on, in different situations with Thad or whatever, you know? We know each other.

ctx.x: Maybe Jimmy Owens and Eddie Daniels. Yeah I remember that, that was nice. I never got a chance to play some of Thad’s music.
